verdicts.reason: The legal hook is real (FAR 16.203-1 and 52.216-4, opened by E). The pain is documented: a May-2026 Lewis Silkin note says most IT contracts' price-variation clauses were written for 3-5% annual moves, not 35-50% jumps (via search snippet). BLS publishes no DRAM-specific PPI; FRED surfaced only the semiconductor-wide and IC-package series. A memory index therefore fills a real gap, and no kill rule applies. The card misses a federal adoption barrier. DLAD 16.203-4 tells contracting officers to pick the most appropriate BLS index, coordinate with the pricing office, and document why each BLS index is unsuitable before using any other (acquisition.gov, via search snippet). Federal adoption is therefore a slow, case-by-case pricing-office decision, and commercial counterparties still default to TrendForce. An index built from distributor list quotes also carries basis risk against the contract prices integrators actually pay.
